author: Independent education critic subagent (Claude Opus 5.5, claude-opus-5-5); did not author these pages; reviewed artifact bytes, manifests, intake, sources list and prerequisite pages only

findings.claim: The Recap and Cheat sheet are visible from first load, under the current activity, and disclose all three answers. render() hides only the activity sections; section.pep-recap (line 645) is never hidden. The cheat sheet gives Activity 1's exact listener line 'const btn = event.target.closest("button.like"); if (!btn) return;' and 'item.textContent = untrusted', Activity 2's full rule '// order: plain code, then microtasks (then, await), then tasks (setTimeout)', and Activity 3's correct branch 'if (!res.ok) { // problem+json? read it and show problem.detail // otherwise show a server message }'. The recap repeats this in prose, including 'show detail for what to fix', which separates C from D.
findings.recommendation: Reveal the recap and cheat sheet only once data-pep-complete is true (keep them in print/no-JS), or make the cheat sheet generic so it doesn't reproduce the option code (no button.like selector, no problem.detail branch).

findings.claim: Activity 2 teaches the full answer rule before the prediction. The 'Two reminders' paragraph sits directly under the code and before the options. It states that the body runs to the first await, that the rest waits as a microtask 'even if the promise was already fulfilled' (this is exactly distractor C's trap), and 'Plain code finishes first, then every microtask, then the next task, such as a timer callback' (distractors D and A). The line 458 instruction 'Commit to an order before you read the reminders under it' can't be enforced: Your task never asks for an early commitment, and the contract requires all instructions before the interaction and 'The learner predicts before any teaching.' The module.json joining detail is only 'an async body runs until its first await'; the rest is the reviewed content itself.
findings.recommendation: Delete the reminders from the teaching region. Put the async-body joining detail in one sentence only if it's truly needed (async-and-await already teaches it), and move the queue rule into hint 2 or the post-check feedback. Remove the 'Commit ... before you read the reminders' sentence.

findings.claim: The 'Where this fits' section precedes the Activity 1 task and states half the answer: 'build items with DOM methods, insert data as text, and let one parent listener handle every item'. That rules out option C (insertAdjacentHTML parses HTML) and points to A's construction before the learner commits. The contract says the fit section 'contains no activity answer.'
findings.recommendation: Keep the authentic decision (untrusted data vs your own fixed markup), but state the good fit without the implementation recipe. For example: 'Any content that comes from visitors or an API, including content that changes after the page loads.' Leave 'as text' and 'one parent listener' to the feedback and recap.

findings.claim: The final hints on Activities 1 and 3 say what separates the correct option from the last distractor, not the next reasoning step. Activity 3 hint 2 says '... which problem details member explains this particular occurrence rather than naming the kind of error', which is the definition of detail as opposed to title and decides C vs D outright. Activity 1 hint 2 (line 418) says 'Rule out any option that still hands visitor text to an API that parses HTML', which eliminates C directly. The contract says a hint 'does not give the answer'.
findings.recommendation: Ask questions that make the learner do the step. Activity 3: 'Read the 400 body in the scenario: which member's value would tell the reviewer what to change?' Activity 1: 'For each option, does the review text pass through anything that builds elements from a string?'

findings.claim: Activity 3 option D is written as 'The same branch as the problem details option, but with showMessage(problem.title).' This marks C as the canonical 'problem details option', so a test-wise learner can narrow to C or D without reasoning about A and B. D also isn't self-contained: in the static alternative and to a screen reader it refers to another option by description, not by letter or content.
findings.recommendation: Write D out as full code (the same block as C with problem.title) so all four options are parallel code blocks. Or make D a different, self-contained misconception, e.g. checking res.status === 400 only and letting the 502 fall through to res.json().

findings.claim: Activities 1 and 3 largely staple together the prerequisite pages' own activities instead of setting new cumulative scenarios. Activity 1's listener bug ('if (event.target.matches("li")) { select(event.target.dataset.id) }' with a nested child, fixed by closest) is the events-and-event-bubbling activity nearly verbatim. The XSS payload '' is the preventing-cross-site-scripting page's own example. Activity 3's '502 with an HTML page shows Check your internet connection' bug and the content-type branch are copied from handling-http-errors-and-problemdetail-responses. Its Vite import.meta.env and Spring Boot framing play no part in any option, so the environment-settings and calling-your-spring-boot-api prerequisites aren't actually reviewed.
findings.recommendation: Change the surface and add one interaction between topics that no single page showed. For example: delegation where the Like button contains an icon span, so closest must skip two levels; a review title set through setAttribute("title") vs innerHTML in a template literal; or in Activity 3, make the API base address matter (e.g. a missing VITE_ prefix gives undefined/reviews) as one of the distractors, so the env topic is genuinely retrieved.

findings.claim: Activity 1 teaches a heavier load in one step than it needs to. The learner must hold two bug reports, a string-built innerHTML line with concatenated quotes, and four multi-clause options that each combine construction and listener changes. Options A, C and D run to 35-45 words, mostly repeated ('Build each item with createElement, using setAttribute for data-id and textContent for the review text') across three options. That repeated prefix forces careful diffing rather than reasoning.
findings.recommendation: Factor out the shared part. Present options as a 2x2 of construction (textContent vs insertAdjacentHTML) by listener (closest vs currentTarget vs unchanged), or show the shared construction once and vary only the listener line in code blocks.

findings.claim: The Markdown companion doesn't mirror the HTML. Under '## Cheat sheet' it lists every hint as unlabelled 'Where to act / Next step' text, hint-2 summaries come out as 'Another hint Another hint, 2 of 2 for Activity N' (lines 92, 102, 112), hint-1 summaries are dropped, sources have no heading, and the fit, task and success-criteria blocks are missing. The contract says 'Headings and objectives match the HTML exactly'. The same pattern appears in 136 of 245 artifact.md files, so this is likely a generator issue.
findings.recommendation: Raise this with tooling and fix the Markdown generator so hints render inside each activity with their labels and a Sources heading is added. No page edit is needed beyond regenerating.
